properties.name: Immutable dependencies
properties.proposed_property: For every successfully factory-created raffle, factory(), quoteToken(), vrfWrapper(), callbackGasLimit(), and requestConfirmations() remain fixed to its implementation/factory configuration; sponsor, sponsorRecipient, treasury, prize, reserve and endTime never change after successful initialization. Only the fixed factory implementation is cloned; no recurring call can replace these identities or configuration.
properties.reasoning: Factory constructor installs its own Raffle implementation; Raffle constructor binds factory to deployer and quoteToken to its argument, while the base embeds the wrapper and LINK identities. Clone-specific configuration has one write path in initialize. No target-changing setter was found by Q01/Q07/Q09.
assumptions: Only canonical factory-created clones are covered; an arbitrary third-party proxy pointing at the implementation is not a registered raffle.
The deployment supplies authentic canonical dependencies and a usable treasury; address immutability is not immutability of external code or policy.
properties.uncertainty: No deployed code, quote implementation, wrapper implementation, deployment provenance, or external governance was inspected. Code presence, six decimals, and link() return do not authenticate identity. Compiler/bytecode/storage checks are deferred.
properties.future_check: Snapshot all identities/configuration after creation; vary every public call and callback, then compare. Create two clones and check shared code immutables but isolated mutable storage.

properties.name: Initialization
properties.proposed_property: The implementation rejects initialize. A fresh canonical clone accepts initialize exactly once, only from its immutable factory. Successful createRaffle produces exactly one initialized registered Active clone with consistent forward/reverse registries and validated positive reserve/future end (at most 30 days); any failed creation leaves factory counters, registrations and asset changes unchanged.
properties.reasoning: Factory validates before cloning, initializes before the prize call, records all three registry entries, and checks final escrow and Active state. initialized is written before the initialization destination queries; any revert rolls it back. The clone has no transaction gap for another caller to initialize.
assumptions: Factory constructor and canonical creation path succeed under ordinary EVM transaction atomicity.
Fresh clone storage starts zero; do not substitute direct implementation storage for clone storage.
properties.uncertainty: initialize does not independently repeat all reserve/end/code/decimals validation; the actual property relies on the immutable canonical factory. No deployed-clone runtime, storage layout, or compiler proof was obtained.
properties.future_check: Exercise nonfactory, repeated, implementation and failed initialization; fail at each createRaffle external boundary and compare pre/post registry state.

properties.name: Prize escrow
properties.proposed_property: A successful canonical creation ends Active and reports ownerOf(configured prize ID)==clone. AwaitingPrize becomes Active only on the configured prize contract's callback with exact sponsor/from, factory/operator, and token ID. Under an honest transferable ERC721, the configured prize remains escrowed until one authorized terminal release, whose reported final owner equals the intended recipient.
properties.reasoning: Factory requires deployed prize code and claimed ERC721 support, safe-transfers the exact prize, then reads owner and raffle status. Winner/sponsor prize paths write prizeClaimed before transfer and verify ownerOf afterward.
assumptions: Prize token truthfully implements ownership and transfers and cannot arbitrarily confiscate the escrowed token.
Sponsor holds/authorizes the selected prize; safeTransferFrom semantics are truthful.
properties.uncertainty: An arbitrary prize contract can lie in supportsInterface, callback and ownerOf. Neither interface screening nor a post-transfer query proves economic value or future transferability. Inherited L-T02 and the DESIGN/interface trust discrepancy remain conditional/documentary, not a new exploit.
properties.future_check: Model honest prizes separately from adversarial callbacks, lying ownerOf, missing callback, wrong callback fields, transfer reverts and delivery-no-op cases; distinguish reported ownership from actual external semantics.

properties.name: Quote-token semantics
properties.proposed_property: For an entry purchase of n>0 that commits, the raffle credits exactly n*1,000,000 nominal units; for each successful quote claim it debits and sends exactly that nominal claim. Under exact fee-free, non-rebasing token semantics, actual clone quote balance is at least accountedQuoteBalance at transaction boundaries; equality holds only when there is no unaccounted surplus. Direct token donations never increase sale counts or liabilities.
properties.reasoning: Accounting follows requested amounts; there is no incoming or outgoing balance-delta verification. SafeERC20 propagates call failure and accepts a true response or successful empty response from code-bearing tokens; it does not establish transferred quantities.
assumptions: Canonical quote identity is verified externally, balances do not rebase/confiscate, and successful transfers move the nominal amount.
Recipient or token restrictions may revert; safety-on-failure does not imply eventual claim availability.
properties.uncertainty: Inherited L-T01 remains an external-dependency condition, not a confirmed in-model bug. Exact token semantics and deployed pause/blocklist/upgrade features are unknown. A malicious token's successful no-op is not a detected delivery failure.
properties.future_check: Maintain a nominal-liability ghost ledger with exact-transfer token model; separately use fee/no-op/rebase/false/empty-return/reverting models to expose where the assumption is required.

properties.name: Bearer authorization
properties.proposed_property: At redemption/refund entry, msg.sender must be the current owner of each claimed ticket; original buyer, sponsor, settler, previous owner and approved operator alone cannot directly claim. Settlement never freezes an owner or transfers assets. An authorized ERC721 transfer moves the future claim with the ticket; successful redemption records the then-current owner in winnerRecipient.
properties.reasoning: Redemption reads ownerOf only after range settlement and compares msg.sender; any failed comparison reverts the enclosing settlement. Refund loops perform the same owner check. Settlement stores the winning ticket ID, not its current owner.
assumptions: ERC721 owner and approval storage have only the inspected update paths; caller controls its current address.
properties.uncertainty: An approved operator can transfer a ticket to itself and then redeem as owner, which is ordinary transferable-token authority. No promise is made that an approval cannot indirectly enable claiming. Receiver callbacks can further transfer tickets.
properties.future_check: Transfer before/after callback and settlement; attempt direct claims as buyer, settler, operator and former owner; then transfer via an approved operator and verify only the new owner can claim.

properties.name: Entry ranges
properties.proposed_property: Historical ranges for ticket IDs 1..ticketCount form a non-overlapping contiguous partition of [1,totalEntries]. A purchase of n appends [oldTotal+1,oldTotal+n], increments ticketCount once and never reuses an ID; 0<=ticketCount<=totalEntries<=2^128-1. Transfers/burns preserve ranges and lifetime counters. With a valid winningEntry, exactly one minted historical range contains it; unmapped IDs return [0,0] and cannot settle.
properties.reasoning: Every purchase has n>=1 and an explicit uint128 total cap before incrementing counters. Thus ticketCount cannot overflow independently of the entry cap. Fresh stored intervals are the only range writes, and no claim deletes their history. Maximum nominal gross is below 2^148.
assumptions: No storage mutation outside inspected code; checks apply to reachable canonical-clone states rather than arbitrary fuzzed storage.
properties.uncertainty: There is no on-chain range enumeration; a future harness must track minted IDs. Historical range existence does not establish current ERC721 ownership after a burn.
properties.future_check: Exercise n=1, large n, remaining-cap n, n=0 and cap+1; compare partitions and unique winning-range proofs across transfers and refunds.

properties.name: Sale and draw windows
properties.proposed_property: Purchases commit only while Active and timestamp<endTime. A sold raffle requests once only in Active with endTime<=timestamp<endTime+2 days; success fixes Drawing, drawRequestedAt and the returned request ID. Successful requestDraw spends paidPrice<=msg.value and refunds exactly msg.value-paidPrice to the caller, with zero net use of any pre-existing native surplus; a failing refund/request reverts the entire request.
properties.reasoning: Sales and draw requests use complementary inequalities at endTime. Drawing is installed before the wrapper call; the in-flight flag protects incomplete request state. The second fee calculation is used as actual paidPrice and checked even if the first quote differed. Caller refund uses a checked native call.
assumptions: Timestamp fits uint64 for stored timestamps and advances under the chain's normal rules.
Wrapper returns a valid usable request identifier and accepts the configured native mode, gas and confirmations.
Native conservation excludes independent forced transfers during the transaction.
properties.uncertainty: An off-chain quote is not a reserved fee. The full supplied msg.value is the effective spending ceiling; the wrapper price/liveness and 300,000-gas sufficiency are unmeasured. At remote timestamps >=2^64, timestamp casts are not covered.
properties.future_check: Use end-1/end/end+timeout-1/deadline, no entries, competing requesters, changing quote/paid fee, forced native surplus, exact/excess payment and rejecting refund receiver.

properties.name: Randomness and callbacks
properties.proposed_property: Only the immutable wrapper can enter rawFulfillRandomWords. A decoded callback changes winner state only when not in-flight, status==Drawing, request ID matches, length==1 and timestamp<callbackDeadline. Accepted callback sets winningEntry=(word mod totalEntries)+1 in [1,totalEntries], resolvedAt and NftWon iff totalEntries>=reserveEntries; it does not transfer assets, settle liabilities, read ownership, or change totalEntries. No second callback can overwrite the result.
properties.reasoning: Drawing can be reached only after positive sales and sale closure. Wrong/late/duplicate/in-flight/decoded wrong-length callbacks emit ignored events without economic-state changes; unauthenticated callers revert in the base. The selector-tagged ExtraArgs encodes nativePayment=true. No timestamp/blockhash entropy or custom signature verifier was found.
assumptions: Canonical wrapper/coordinator provides unpredictable, unbiased 256-bit words and authentic request routing; local sender authentication is not a proof of VRF validity.
One successful asynchronous request does not guarantee a timely callback.
properties.uncertainty: Wrapper/coordinator/proof implementation and deployed settings are absent. Modulo sampling is not perfectly uniform for arbitrary N: outcome preimage counts differ by at most one out of 2^256. For N<=2^128-1, total variation from uniform is r(N-r)/(N*2^256)<=N/(4*2^256)<2^-130. No practical exploit is established by that arithmetic. Malformed ABI reverts before the handler.
properties.future_check: Try unauthorized, in-flight, wrong-ID, zero/two-word, repeated and deadline callbacks; test words 0 and 2^256-1 and N near cap. Separate authentication/invariants from external randomness-quality assertions.

properties.name: Refund activation and timeouts
properties.proposed_property: Active empty raffles may enter Refunding before end only at sponsor request and at/after end by anyone. Active sold raffles may do so only at/after end+2 days; Drawing raffles only at/after drawRequestedAt+2 days. Transition moves the entire unsettledPot to remainingRefundLiability once and zeroes unsettledPot. Refunding never returns to a sale or winner state; late callbacks cannot revive it.
properties.reasoning: The callback accepts strictly before its deadline and refunds permit at/after it, so both cannot be valid at the same timestamp. Sold request expiry is also exclusive for requests and inclusive for refunds. Winner states reject enableRefunds.
assumptions: Normal timestamp domain and committed canonical lifecycle transitions.
Someone submits the enabling transaction and owners subsequently submit their claims.
properties.uncertainty: Availability is permissionless eligibility, not automatic execution. No refunds exist after a timely winner result merely because external prize delivery later fails. This preserves inherited prize availability/trust limits.
properties.future_check: Test each state at deadline-1/deadline/deadline+1, sponsor versus outsider on empty raffles, competing cancellation/first purchase and late callbacks after refund activation.

properties.name: Payout conservation
properties.proposed_property: Let G=totalEntries*ENTRY_PRICE, A=unsettledPot+remainingRefundLiability+winnerProceeds+sponsorProceeds+protocolFees, and Paid be cumulative nominal successful quote claims/refunds. At committed transaction boundaries A+Paid==G. Settlement preserves A, sets unsettledPot=0, allocates F=floor(G*500/10000), cash W=floor(G*8000/10000) only in CashWon (otherwise W=0), and sponsor S=G-F-W. Refund activation preserves A. Each successful payout decreases A by exactly its paid nominal amount.
properties.reasoning: One-time settlement transfers nominal pot into disjoint claims and assigns the remainder to sponsor. Price 1,000,000 is divisible by 10,000, so for reachable undonated nominal pots the 5% and 80% allocations have no raw-unit dust at all. G<2^148 and G*8000<2^161, so the reachable mulDiv product fits 256 bits.
assumptions: Paid tracks successful protocol outflows only and is a harness ghost value, not production storage.
No arbitrary storage injection; actual asset sufficiency additionally requires P04 token semantics.
properties.uncertainty: This proves the form of nominal conservation by source reasoning, not executed verification. Do not require contract token balance==G after claims or count donations as sales. The invariant is stated at transaction boundaries, not arbitrary callback observations during partial updates.
properties.future_check: Maintain a per-clone ghost ledger through interleaved independent claims, failed calls, refunds and donations; verify conservation and exact 95/5 or 80/15/5 allocation at settlement.

properties.name: Single claims
properties.proposed_property: Each raffle successfully settles at most once, successfully redeems its winning ticket at most once, and successfully delivers the configured prize at most once across winner/sponsor routes. Every sponsor/treasury/winner quote allocation is consumed at most once. Claims to fixed recipients are permissionless to trigger but cannot be redirected by the caller. Claim failure preserves that claim for later retry.
properties.reasoning: settlementComplete, winnerRedeemed and prizeClaimed guard one-time transitions. Payout variables are zeroed before transfers, winner claims burn, and refund/winner branches are mutually exclusive. No refill path exists after one-time settlement. Prize return in CashWon/Refunding is independent of quote claims.
assumptions: External transfers either truthfully succeed or revert/produce detectable failure; P03/P04 qualify delivery claims.
Terminal status and allocations remain immutable except consumption.
properties.uncertainty: Failure of a separate earlier/later payout is not global rollback of already committed claims. Sponsor and treasury can be paid before winner redemption; blocked winner delivery does not unwind their completed transactions.
properties.future_check: Permute all release orders; repeat each release/settlement/redemption, mix same recipients, and fail individual external sends while comparing only that transaction's state.

properties.name: Refunds and burns
properties.proposed_property: In Refunding, a successful refund batch contains 1..100 existing tickets currently owned by msg.sender, burns each exactly once, pays sum(last-first+1)*ENTRY_PRICE, and decreases remainingRefundLiability by precisely that amount. Remaining liability equals the nominal value of all unburned refund tickets. Duplicate, absent, previously burned or foreign-owned IDs revert the entire batch. Historical ranges, totalEntries and ticketCount remain unchanged.
properties.reasoning: Ownership lookup precedes each burn, so the second occurrence of a duplicate fails _requireOwned and rolls back earlier burns. Batch loop is bounded by tickets, not represented entries. Aggregate refund entries cannot exceed lifetime entries on valid unique IDs.
assumptions: No prior winner redemption can coexist with Refunding; ERC721 burns clear ownership and approvals as inspected.
Actual quote received requires P04; current holder may differ from buyer.
properties.uncertainty: A 100-ticket bound does not prove a concrete gas limit. Ranges remain accessible after burns but are not redeemable ownership. Contract owners need a way to invoke refundTickets.
properties.future_check: Use 0/1/100/101 ticket batches; duplicate early/late, nonexistent and foreign IDs; quote-send failures; owner transfers followed by refunds and repeated refunds.

properties.name: Rollback and reentrancy
properties.proposed_property: A guarded economic call that reverts rolls back its entire call subtree, including prior nested external state changes; if that revert propagates to the transaction top level, the whole transaction rolls back. During a guarded function, other functions using that same instance's guard cannot execute recursively. Successful reentrant unguarded ERC721 actions must still satisfy ownership/destination checks and cannot duplicate quote/NFT liabilities. Fulfillment during the wrapper request call is ignored until the request ID is persisted.
properties.reasoning: The guard rejects only ENTERED==2, so initial clone guard value zero still blocks recursive entry after the first function writes 2 and later resets to 1. Claim effects precede external sends; SafeERC20, ERC721 receiver rejection, native refund failure and owner postcheck failures bubble reverts. initialize sets initialized before external view queries; prize receiver checks its exact phase.
assumptions: Standard EVM nested-call/transaction rollback and the supplied dependency source behavior.
External tokens cannot create irreversible off-chain side effects that EVM rollback would undo.
properties.uncertainty: Inherited transfers/approvals, raw fulfillment and onERC721Received are not blanket nonReentrant. A safe-mint recipient may transfer the ticket during its callback, so ownerOf(ticketId)==original recipient on return is NOT a valid invariant. During an ordinary inherited safeTransferFrom with no guard already entered, its new owner may legitimately redeem/refund/burn inside the receiver callback. Read-only intermediate observations are possible. No dynamic adversarial-callback campaign ran. A caller that catches a low-level revert can retain unrelated outer-transaction effects; rollback assertions must use the correct call boundary.
properties.future_check: Exercise quote/prize/receiver/native-refund callback edges; compare reverted whole transactions; permit authorized nested transfers and ordinary safe-transfer receiver claims, while checking ledger and one-time claims rather than universal callback rejection.

properties.name: Destinations and isolation
properties.proposed_property: At each screening call, nonzero ticket destinations and quote payout recipients must not equal self, canonical factory, quote token, wrapper, configured prize token, factory implementation, or a code-bearing raffle registered by that same factory. Initialization screens sponsor, sponsorRecipient and treasury; creation also screens prize selection and sponsorRecipient. Burns to zero remain allowed. Payout callers cannot choose alternate recipients.
properties.reasoning: All ticket updates funnel through the override; quote transfers share _transferQuote. Registry screening is explicitly against IRaffleFactory(factory), and skips the registry for code-less addresses. Fixed prize recipients derive from already-screened initialization or ticket ownership.
assumptions: Canonical factory registry is truthful and its clone addresses retain code.
A recipient outside the enumerated set is responsible for being able to operate its ticket and receive/recover assets.
properties.uncertainty: The property is local to same-factory plumbing, not universal all-contract recoverability or all-factory isolation. Cross-factory clones and arbitrary incapable contracts are not generally recognized. Outgoing prize uses transferFrom rather than receiver acceptance. Inherited cross-factory scope lead stays unresolved; DESIGN's broader wording is reserved for S5.
properties.future_check: Exercise all forbidden addresses through buy/mint/transfer/quote/creation, same-factory clones, another factory's clone, code-less and contract recipients. Characterize acceptance separately from a specification failure verdict.

properties.name: ERC721 and clone inheritance
properties.proposed_property: Canonical clones preserve inherited ERC721 owner/approval/balance rules and receiver checks while routing mint/transfer/burn through the raffle destination override. Transfers/burns clear per-token approval; absent/burned ownerOf and tokenURI revert. name/symbol remain fixed despite skipped ERC721 constructor storage on clones; valid tokenURI returns empty with the inherited empty base URI. ERC165 reports IERC165, IERC721 and metadata support. Clones share fixed implementation code/immutables but not token/lifecycle/guard storage.
properties.reasoning: The project overrides _update only to screen destinations then calls super. Constant metadata overrides avoid relying on implementation constructor strings. Factory uses only the unsalted clone(address) path, which embeds the fixed implementation and does not expose an upgrade slot. Inherited wrapper getters/raw callback are part of the actual surface even though IRaffle does not redeclare them all.
assumptions: Compiled inheritance/dispatch implements the inspected Solidity semantics; ordinary minimal-proxy delegatecall storage isolation.
properties.uncertainty: No slither-check-erc, compiler linearization/storage inspection, runtime dispatch test or bytecode check occurred. Destination restrictions intentionally qualify generic unrestricted-transfer expectations; this is not full ERC721 conformance certification. Imported unused extension/helper functions are not additional production entrypoints.
properties.future_check: After sealing, check supported ERC721 interfaces and inherited overloads, approvals/clearing, safe receiver failures, empty metadata, two-clone state isolation and guard initialization with actual compiled code.

properties.proposed_property: After the independently proceeding S5 is available, each normative DESIGN/interface requirement must map to an actual source transition/property, explicit assumption, or supported mismatch. The candidate requirements include atomic escrow, fixed economics, owner-controlled burn/delivery rollback, deadline inequalities, storage-only settlement and isolation. Until then, property documentation must not present full specification compliance as established.
properties.reasoning: P01-P15 express the source-side obligations and limits for later comparison. The permitted FIRST-PASS explicitly says specification compliance is INCOMPLETE and supplies no verdict; this continuation preserves that statement. Existing prize-trust wording discrepancy and cross-factory scope lead are inherited, not newly resolved here.

DESIGN is a candidate requirement source; implementation establishes actual behavior.

properties.future_check: Parent may map the independently sealed S5 requirements to these exact evidence references and proposed properties in a later authorized phase.

manual_review.analysis: Private _ticketRanges is exposed through ticketRange and purchase events; ticket ownership, purchase amounts, raffle parameters and winning entry are observable. Random words are supplied as public transaction calldata on fulfillment; privacy is not what prevents advance selection. No secret-dependent raffle branch, commitment/reveal protocol or confidentiality guarantee was found. Library salt/private/keccak hits belong to unused deterministic clone helpers, formatting or storage constants.
manual_review.assumptions_and_limits: Unpredictability before fulfillment depends on the external VRF path. No participant anonymity, private mempool behavior or frontend secrecy was assessed. Absence of local commit-reveal is not a finding by itself.

manual_review.analysis: Pending buys can change assigned intervals, final ownership probabilities and whether reserve is met; buyer pays fixed per-entry price but cannot constrain final totalEntries or branch. Purchasing is forbidden at/after sale end, before requests become valid, so a local buyer cannot add entries after an accepted draw request. Empty-raffle sponsor cancellation and first purchase race by ordering: cancellation first makes buy fail; purchase first removes the pre-end empty-cancellation condition. At draw/callback deadlines the inequalities are disjoint. Front-running permissionless settlement cannot redirect ownership or payouts, though the losing duplicate settlement reverts. Ticket transfer/redeem races follow current ownership and ordinary granted ERC721 authority. Off-chain VRF price quotes can become stale; msg.value bounds the actual fee and excess is refunded atomically. Competing requesters can waste revert gas but cannot create two committed requests.
manual_review.assumptions_and_limits: No fixed-odds or branch guarantee exists in buyEntries. Claiming one from an off-chain quote would be a conditional integration error, not a source-confirmed exploit. Block inclusion/censorship can affect eligibility at boundaries; no external MEV strategy, marketplace or frontend behavior was examined. Authorized operators can move bearer claims before revocation.

manual_review.analysis: Local authentication is exact msg.sender equality with the immutable wrapper. Winning entry depends on one supplied word and frozen entry count, not timestamp/blockhash. A successful request cannot be rerolled locally; terminal/late/duplicate callback guards prevent rewriting the outcome. The application contains no signature/permit/replay-nonce scheme, ecrecover, tx.origin authorization or dynamic packed-message hash. ExtraArgs uses a fixed selector tag and ABI encoding. Imported CREATE2 hashes, address checksum/bytes equality helpers, and Math modExp/packed precompile arguments are not raffle authentication or randomness paths. Modulo output preimage counts differ by at most one; P08 gives the explicit negligible-bias bound instead of claiming perfect uniformity.
manual_review.assumptions_and_limits: No VRF proof verification, wrapper/coordinator implementation, key security, live configuration or callback gas measurement was available. Timely fulfillment, honest randomness and no selective withholding remain external assumptions; timeout refunds are the documented liveness fallback.

manual_review.analysis: No project AMM swap, lending/borrowing, reserve-price read, price-feed query, flash-loan callback or balance-based vote/reward input was located. Byte swaps and an Uniswap credit in library comments are not DeFi integrations. Entry price and payout ratios are constants; donation/temporary balance changes do not alter totalEntries or nominal liabilities. A buy made before end cannot also draw/redeem that newly purchased claim in the same transaction under one timestamp: request requires timestamp>=end while buy requires timestamp<end. Existing matured bearer claims can be acquired/redeemed by external integrations, but this source supplies no flash-borrow callback or duplicated claim path. There IS an external oracle/service boundary: wrapper fee quoting plus VRF; the wrapper interface declares linkNativeFeed although Raffle does not call it.
manual_review.assumptions_and_limits: Do not conclude 'no oracle risk' or 'flash loans impossible.' Wrapper pricing/feed/proof internals and external credit/marketplace arrangements are absent. Fee failure, bad randomness or withholding are dependency/liveness assumptions; canonical quote semantics remain inherited L-T01.

new_continuation_evidence.title: Callback-safe properties must allow valid bearer actions
new_continuation_evidence.statement: Safe-mint ownership need not remain with the original recipient after its callback, and ordinary inherited safe-transfer receivers can claim/burn while no economic guard is already entered. The appropriate assertions are authorization, conservation and single use, not a blanket ban on callbacks.

new_continuation_evidence.title: Exact nominal allocation and bounded modulo bias
new_continuation_evidence.statement: Reachable pots are multiples of 1,000,000, so 5% and 80% produce exact raw-unit allocations; current cap also puts mulDiv products below 2^161. Modulo randomness is extremely close to uniform under a uniform 256-bit source, but not exactly uniform for all entry counts.

new_continuation_evidence.title: A fixed entry-price quote does not fix odds or reserve outcome
